sections.offseason:
**Both teams changed head coaches, and both reach Sunday night leaning on the run with a quarterback they did not plan on in August.** Baltimore went 8-9 and missed the playoffs in 2025; John Harbaugh left for the Giants and Jesse Minter took over as head coach and defensive play-caller, with Declan Doyle running the offense. The big spend was on the edge: Trey Hendrickson signed for four years and about $112 million after a Maxx Crosby trade fell through on a physical. He is out for the second straight week after finger surgery.
- **This week's moves in Baltimore:** with Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn on IR, the Ravens traded with Philadelphia for Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens on Oct. 7, and Jurgens has already been ruled out (concussion). TE Durham Smythe tore an Achilles and went to IR Wednesday; Nick Vannett was signed up from the practice squad. Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane is on IR (wrist).
- **Atlanta fired Raheem Morris and GM Terry Fontenot and hired Kevin Stefanski** (GM Ian Cunningham). Michael Penix Jr. was coming back from the torn left ACL that ended his 2025, so Cooper Rush started Weeks 1 and 2: two losses, 16 points, four Rush interceptions and zero red-zone trips. Penix is 2-0 since (35-14 at Green Bay, 45-24 at New Orleans). Tua Tagovailoa signed a one-year deal in March and is the No. 2.
- **Backfield:** Brian Robinson Jr. signed a one-year, $2.5 million deal to replace Tyler Allgeier (to Arizona) after 92 carries for 400 yards as a 49ers reserve in 2025. He has four touchdowns in the last two games.
- **The Falcons' pass rush was rebuilt on the fly:** Jalon Walker tore an ACL Aug. 6 (out for the season) and James Pearce Jr. is serving an eight-game suspension (eligible Nov. 2). Za'Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas were added and Brandon Dorlus is back after 8.5 sacks; Atlanta still leads the league in pressures. CB A.J. Terrell Jr. is on IR.
sections.matchup:
**Baltimore's offense runs into the one thing Atlanta does best, and it does it without Lamar Jackson.** The Falcons have allowed 193 rushing yards on 71 carries (2.7 a carry, 48.3 a game, fewest in the league) and two rushing touchdowns, both Alvin Kamara runs from the 3 and the 5. Opponents throw 44 times a game against them instead: 276.5 passing yards a game and seven passing touchdowns, three to tight ends (Pat Freiermuth, Darren Waller twice). All nine touchdowns allowed came in the red zone (9 of 16 trips).
- **Henry is the Ravens' scoring:** 7 of their 14 offensive touchdowns and 11 of the team's 13 carries inside the 5 (Jackson had the other two), with six scores on those 11. Baltimore is 11 of 15 in the red zone. But Henry ran 3.4 and 3.2 a carry the last two weeks, and with Jurgens out rookie Olaivavega Ioane stays at center and Andrew Vorhees (questionable) is the swing guard.
- **Huntley changes the passing tree, not the goal line.** Jackson has nine completions of 25-plus yards; Huntley had one in his two 2025 starts and went 8 of 9 for 63 in the second half against Tennessee. Ravens red-zone targets: Zay Flowers 4, Mark Andrews 3, Rashod Bateman 2, Lane 2 and Smythe 1 (both IR), Chris Moore 1, Matthew Hibner 1. With Lane and Smythe gone the tight ends hold a third of what remains, against a defense that hands tight ends touchdowns.
- **Pressure:** Atlanta leads the NFL with 79 pressures and is second with 35 quarterback hits but has seven sacks; Huntley's legs turn pressure into scrambles and checkdowns.
- **Atlanta's offense with Penix:** 33 of 45, 479 yards, 10.6 an attempt, 80 points, 8 of 10 in the red zone, and 7 of those 8 red-zone touchdowns were runs. Bijan Robinson has 6 of the 7 carries inside the 5 (scores from the 3, 2 and 4); Brian Robinson Jr. scored from the 7, 4, 8 and 11. Drake London has 16 of Penix's 45 targets, zero red-zone targets and zero touchdowns this season; Austin Hooper's 5-yard catch is the only red-zone tight end target that scored.
- **Baltimore's run defense:** 3.9 a carry, 16th in EPA per rush (SI), no 100-yard rusher in 18 straight games (ESPN). Backs have four rushing touchdowns against it, and the Ravens have allowed touchdowns on 9 of 14 red-zone trips. Backs have 16 catches for 37 yards against them, so Bijan's two targets a game with Penix stay small. Mike Green starts for Hendrickson, Marlon Humphrey is questionable, and outside receivers have hurt them: Carnell Tate 145, CeeDee Lamb 112.
sections.injuries:
**Friday report (Oct 9): final designations.** Ravens: QB Lamar Jackson (left ankle) **Out** after not practicing all week; Minter named Tyler Huntley the starter, and Joe Fagnano is the backup (Skylar Thompson is on IR). OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) **Out** for the second straight week; Mike Green starts. C Cam Jurgens (concussion) **Out** days after the trade. WR Zay Flowers (foot) **Questionable** after limited practices all week, on top of the hamstring that cost him Week 2; CB Marlon Humphrey (calf/hamstring) and G Andrew Vorhees are **Questionable**. Rashod Bateman (shoulder) and Chris Moore (ankle) were full Thursday with no designation; Ronnie Stanley and Kyle Hamilton carry none.
- **Ravens on IR:** TE Durham Smythe (Achilles, season), WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist; Minter says he is "doing really well"), C Ethan Pocic, G Jovaughn Gwyn, QB Skylar Thompson, CB T.J. Tampa, CB Bilhal Kone, S Jahquez Robinson, RB Adam Randall.
- **Falcons:** LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) **Out**. LT Jake Matthews (groin) **Questionable**: he left Monday's game, returned to practice Thursday and would make his 200th straight start; Michael Jerrell is next. Edge Za'Darius Smith (concussion/neck, team-high 2.5 sacks), LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) and edge Samson Ebukam (hamstring) are **Questionable**. No Falcons skill player carries a designation.
- **Falcons on IR/out:** CB A.J. Terrell Jr., OLB Jalon Walker (ACL, season), DL Da'Shawn Hand, LB JD Bertrand, RB Trey Sermon, WR Beaux Collins, OT Cameron Williams; OLB James Pearce Jr. is suspended; OT Storm Norton, DT Anterio Thompson and LB DeAngelo Malone are out.
- **Where the touches go:** Jackson's 19 carries (4.75 a game) and his two carries inside the 5 come off the board; Henry gets the designed runs (24 carries projected) and Huntley the scrambles. If Flowers is inactive, his 7 targets a game go to Bateman first (9 targets in Week 2, the game Flowers missed) and Andrews second (7 that day), and Bateman's touchdown read rises from 14% to about 19%. Smythe's in-line snaps go to Hibner and Vannett. On the Atlanta side nothing moves: every pass catcher and both backs are healthy.
- **Verify at inactives (6:50 p.m. ET Sunday):** Flowers, Humphrey, Vorhees, Matthews and Za'Darius Smith. Mercedes-Benz Stadium has a retractable roof (63°F and dry outside): weather is a non-factor.
sections.oddsNotes:
**The biggest quarterback move on the board: seven and a half points through zero.** The lookahead had Baltimore -6 (SI); DraftKings opened BAL -4.5 with a 48.5 total and moneylines of Ravens -218 / Falcons +180. It flipped after Jackson's midweek DNPs, and Friday's ruling took it to ATL -3 (-122; BAL +3 at +102), total 43.5 (-110 both ways), moneylines -180 / +150. Earlier in the week DraftKings had ATL -3 (-108) and -162 / +136, so the juice and the moneyline are still walking toward 3.5.
- De-vigged, the moneyline is **61.6% Atlanta / 38.4% Baltimore**; ESPN's FPI has Atlanta at 59.9%.
- Implied team totals: 23.25 Atlanta, 20.25 Baltimore. The total has dropped five points with the quarterback.
- Baltimore is 1-3 against the spread, Atlanta 2-2; the over is 2-2 for both. Since 2019 the Ravens are 6-11 without Jackson and score 17.6 a game; Huntley has five of those six wins and went 2-0 as a fill-in last year.
- The desk projects **Falcons 24, Ravens 17**. The side is a 1: the move already prices Jackson, Jurgens and Hendrickson, and Huntley's Ravens tend to stay close, but Henry against a 2.7-a-carry run defense is the matchup Baltimore loses. The total is the stronger lean at 2: both teams want to run, the projection has 59 offensive plays a side, and Baltimore's passing game loses its explosives. The risk is Bijan's breakaways and Penix's 10.6 an attempt.
- **Props on the main numbers:** Bijan Robinson rushing 87.5 (DraftKings, over -114; FanDuel 89.5) against a 101 projection; Penix passing 219.5 (DraftKings) / 224.5 (FanDuel) against 200; Andrews receiving 32.5 (DraftKings, over -115) against 42. Bijan's receiving yards (26.5 at DraftKings) against a 17 projection is the fourth: Baltimore has allowed 37 receiving yards to backs all season. Henry's 78.5 (DraftKings) / 79.5 (FanDuel) against the projection's 88 is not a desk lean: that 88 caps Atlanta's run-defense factor at 0.85, and the real number is worse.

sections.offseason:
**Buffalo changed head coaches and traded for a No. 1 receiver; Los Angeles went all-in on its pass rush and lost the centrepiece to knee surgery.** The Bills fired Sean McDermott in January after the Divisional Round loss to Denver and promoted offensive coordinator Joe Brady (36, five-year deal); Jim Leonhard is the new defensive coordinator. Buffalo sent its 2026 second-round pick (No. 60) to Chicago for DJ Moore on March 11 and signed edge Bradley Chubb to a three-year deal.
- **The Rams sent Jared Verse, a 2027 first, a 2028 second and a 2029 third to Cleveland for Myles Garrett,** and Garrett had arthroscopic knee surgery after Week 1; he is on injured reserve and eligible to return in Week 6. Aaron Donald unretired after the trade on a one-year, $20 million deal; he missed Week 4 with a back injury and practiced in full Friday.
- **The Rams rebuilt the secondary from Kansas City:** Trent McDuffie (trade and extension) and Jaylen Watson (signed), with Emmanuel Forbes Jr. added since. Matthew Stafford is the reigning MVP.
- **Injuries have already reshaped both skill groups.** Puka Nacua missed Weeks 2 and 3 (hip) and came back with 9 catches for 125 yards and a rushing touchdown at Philadelphia; second-year TE Terrance Ferguson went to IR (ankle) after Week 3. Moore has played through an AC joint sprain since Week 2 and left Week 4 before halftime; Joshua Palmer is out Monday and rookie Skyler Bell makes his NFL debut.
- The last meeting, in 2024 at SoFi, was a 44-42 Rams win in which Josh Allen accounted for six touchdowns. Buffalo is 3-1 after a 29-26 home loss to New England; the Rams are 2-2 after a 24-20 win at Philadelphia.
sections.matchup:
**Josh Allen is Buffalo's goal-line back, and he draws the best defense on the field.** Allen has seven rushing touchdowns in four games, six of them from the 1 or the 2: six carries inside the 5, six scores. James Cook III has 13 red-zone carries (tied for the game high) but only four inside the 5, with scores from the 1, 3 and 8. Buffalo is 11 of 16 in the red zone and 10 of its 16 touchdowns came on the ground.
- **The Rams allow 247.5 yards a game and 4.8 yards per pass attempt**, rank third in EPA per play, and have allowed seven offensive touchdowns: six to wide receivers and one quarterback run. Backs have no touchdowns against them on 87 carries (4.1 a carry) and 27 targets; tight ends are 12 of 29 for 85 yards. Opponents are 7 of 12 in the red zone. Garrett is out; Byron Young had 2.5 sacks last week and Donald returns.
- **Buffalo's receiver room is thin.** Palmer is out and Moore (shoulder) is questionable after one noncontact practice; neither book has posted a Moore prop. Khalil Shakir has 23 targets, five red-zone looks and no touchdown; Keon Coleman went 6 for 116 and a score last week after Moore left and has two targets inside the 10. Dalton Kincaid's targets have gone 6, 8, 3, 2. Cook has 10 targets and Ty Johnson 6; Dawson Knox has the only tight-end touchdown, from the 1.
- **The Rams gain 417 yards a game but score 21.3 points** because of eight turnovers (six Stafford interceptions) and 8 of 15 in the red zone. Stafford threw 55 and 51 times the last two weeks. Kyren Williams has 13 red-zone carries, three inside the 5 (two scores), four touchdowns, and 20 targets in the last two games. Davante Adams leads the team with 38 targets and four red-zone targets, none inside the 10; with Nacua active he is 7 for 58 on 15 targets, without him 15 for 332 and both of his touchdowns.
- **Buffalo's defense is the soft side:** 372 yards a game, 7.5 yards per attempt, ten passing touchdowns (six to receivers, three to backs, one to a tight end), 11 of 16 red-zone trips allowed for touchdowns, and 30th in EPA per play. Backs have six touchdowns against it (three rushing, three receiving) on 6.8 targets a game, though only 3.8 yards a carry. Ed Oliver is out, nickel Dee Alford is questionable and Christian Benford returns.
- **Tight ends:** with Ferguson on IR, Tyler Higbee took 11 and 6 targets; Colby Parkinson is back with two inside-the-10 targets in three games, restoring the Rams' three-tight-end sets.

sections.offseason:
**Chicago is in year two of Ben Johnson's build and on its third quarterback in five weeks.** Caleb Williams strained his right hamstring (Grade 2) against Minnesota on Sep 20 and has not played since; Case Keenum beat Philadelphia 27-7 and Tyson Bagent beat the Jets 23-12 in his first start since 2023 (25 of 34, 268 yards, no touchdowns, one interception). Johnson named Bagent the Week 5 starter on Monday; Williams returned to a limited practice Friday and is listed questionable, with Keenum the expected backup.
- **DJ Moore was traded to Buffalo in March** for a second-round pick (No. 60), which moved Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and slot veteran Kalif Raymond into the top three and made Colston Loveland the move tight end. Rookies Dillon Thieneman (S), Sam Roush (TE), Zavion Thomas (WR) and Keyshaun Elliott (LB) are on the two-deep (draft slots verify).
- **The Bears lead the NFL in total yards (429.0 a game), rushing (196.3) and possession time (36:35)**, and beat Green Bay 31-27 in last season's Wild Card round; a win Sunday would be their third straight over the Packers, the first such run since 2005-06.
- **Green Bay lost its defensive coordinator and its two best defenders.** Jeff Hafley left to coach Miami and Jonathan Gannon took over with a 3-4 base; Micah Parsons is still on PUP after the ACL he tore Dec 14, and Edgerrin Cooper went to IR on Oct 6 (Achilles). Josh Jacobs has been on the commissioner exempt list since Aug 30, Jayden Reed had season-ending neck surgery, and RT Zach Bako-Bewele is on IR (knee).
- Tucker Kraft signed a four-year, $75 million extension on Sep 12; Jonnu Smith is the second tight end. The Packers are 2-2 (22-39 at Minnesota, 20-17 at the Jets in overtime, 14-35 against Atlanta, 17-14 at Tampa Bay) and have been outscored by 32.
sections.matchup:
**Chicago's run game against a Packers front that has allowed a running-back touchdown in every game is the card.** The Bears have run 159 times for 785 yards (4.9 a carry); Green Bay allows 139.3 rushing yards a game and seven rushing touchdowns, all seven to backs, and opponents have scored touchdowns on 12 of 14 red-zone trips. Cooper is gone from the second level and Javon Hargrave (toe) is questionable.
- **Kyle Monangai's goal-line role is vacated.** He had 6 of Chicago's 15 running-back carries inside the 5 and both Week 4 touchdowns; D'Andre Swift had the other 8 (two scores, both in Week 1, then a fumble at the Minnesota 1, a loss from the Philadelphia 1 and two Week 4 goal-line scores reversed on replay). Roschon Johnson moves to No. 2; the sneak is live (Keenum scored from the 1 in Week 3).
- **The Bears' red zone is 8 for 19 (2 for 7 against the Jets).** Burden and Loveland have six red-zone targets each, Raymond four, Odunze two. Bagent's Week 4 tree was Loveland 9 targets, Odunze 7, Burden 6, Raymond 2, and he has no touchdown passes on 43 attempts.
- **Green Bay's pass defense is sounder than its run defense:** 6.9 yards per attempt allowed, 7.7 yards per target to receivers and 5.5 to tight ends (17 of 24 for 133). Ten sacks in four games without Parsons or Cooper.
- **Every Green Bay touchdown this season has been a pass.** Jordan Love has two touchdown passes in all four games (87 of 154, 1,041 yards, 8 TD, 3 INT) and a 113.2 career rating against Chicago; the run game is last at 58.0 yards a game (73 carries, 232 yards) and the backs have no rushing touchdowns. Christian Watson has 4 of the 8 scores and seven red-zone targets, and all three of his targets inside the 5 scored. Matthew Golden leads with 37 targets and scored from the 15 and the 2 the last two weeks; Kraft drew two targets inside the 3 at Tampa.
- **Chicago has allowed 28 points in three games** and 23.7% on third down (second), and its ball control holds opponents to 48 plays a game. Tight ends have 13 catches on 22 targets for 139 yards and no touchdowns against it; receivers get 9.2 yards a target, inflated by Carolina's 353 passing yards in Week 1. Kyler Gordon and Anthony Johnson Jr. are out of the secondary.
- **Green Bay's interior line is patched again:** Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk are doubtful and Jager Burton questionable. Love has been sacked once in two weeks after seven in the first two.

**Cincinnati spent the offseason buying a defense; Miami tore everything down.** The Bengals sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants for DT Dexter Lawrence II and extended him, then signed S Bryan Cook (three years, $40.25M), S Kyle Dugger (one year), DT Jonathan Allen and EDGE Boye Mafe; Al Golden is in year two as coordinator. Joe Burrow is back from an eight-game 2025, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both under contract.
- **Miami fired Mike McDaniel after a 7-10 season** and hired Jeff Hafley from Green Bay's defensive staff, with Jon-Eric Sullivan as general manager. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill and Bradley Chubb were released, Jaylen Waddle was traded to Denver and Minkah Fitzpatrick to the Jets, and Malik Willis signed for three years and $67.5M. The draft added WRs Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell and OT Kadyn Proctor, who is starting at left guard.
- **De'Von Achane tore an ACL in Week 3** and is on IR for the season; Ollie Gordon II has been the lead back since, with Jaylen Wright splitting when healthy.
- **The Bengals are 2-2 and have lost two straight,** 30-27 in Pittsburgh and 22-17 to Jacksonville, after opening 33-27 over Tampa Bay and 20-6 in Houston. Andrei Iosivas and CB Jalen Davis are on IR; WR Mitchell Tinsley came off Houston's practice squad and caught 3 for 49 in his debut.
- **Miami is 0-4 and has not scored more than 13 points:** 27-13 at Las Vegas, 35-13 at San Francisco, 24-10 to Kansas City and 15-10 at Minnesota. Both teams have their bye in Week 6.

The pass rush has 4 sacks in four games, all of them last week, and DE Robert Beal Jr. is out. Storm Duck, Reese Taylor and Darrell Baker Jr. are all out at corner.
- **Miami bleeds to backs and tight ends, not wideouts.** Seven of the 11 offensive touchdowns it has allowed went to running backs or a fullback (3 rushing, 4 receiving), two to tight ends, one to a receiver. Tight ends catch 7.3 of 7.8 targets a game for 83 yards; backs catch 5 for 42. Backs run 25.8 times a game at 3.85 a carry.

**Cleveland is 3-1 under Todd Monken on three straight one-score wins, and it has had ten days off.** The Browns lost 34-10 at Jacksonville in Week 1, then beat Tampa Bay 23-19, Carolina 21-18 and Pittsburgh 27-24 on Thursday night, Oct 1. Myles Garrett was traded to the Rams in the offseason with Jared Verse coming back, and Deshaun Watson has started all four games after missing 2025: 80 of 115 for 855 yards, 6 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Shedeur Sanders is the backup; Dillon Gabriel is on IR.
- **The Browns' receiving tree is two rookies and a second-year tight end:** KC Concepcion (28 targets, team high), Harold Fannin Jr. (23) and Denzel Boston (22 targets, 284 yards, 21.8 a catch). Jerry Jeudy has 8 targets in four games.
- **New York is 1-3 in Aaron Glenn's second year and has lost three straight:** 20-17 in overtime to Green Bay, 31-24 at Detroit, 23-12 at Chicago. Geno Smith is 85 of 117 for 902 yards, 5 touchdowns and no interceptions; rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq is the second option behind Garrett Wilson.
- **The Jets' skill group keeps shrinking:** Breece Hall (quad) misses a second straight game, Adonai Mitchell (finger) a third, and WRs Arian Smith, Omar Cooper Jr. and Tim Patrick are on IR. TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is back off the report; he has not had a target since Week 1.

- **That is Braelon Allen's opening.** Allen took all 14 back carries at Chicago and inherits Hall's four carries inside the 5; he already scored from the 5 against Green Bay. The catch is the Jets' line: LG Dylan Parham is out, Jordan Meredith starts, and Smith has been sacked 12 times.

Wilson drew 17 of 52 targets (33%) in the two games without Mitchell and has two of New York's five passing scores (from the 5 and the 23). The Jets are 6 of 11 in the red zone; touchdowns have gone to Hall, Allen, Sadiq (a 3-yard run and a 24-yard catch), Ruckert (from the 4), Wilson twice and Isaiah Williams.
- **Cleveland's pass defense is the softer side:** nine passing touchdowns allowed (four by Trevor Lawrence), 8.8 yards per target to receivers, and 36 targets to tight ends with three tight-end scores.
- **Cleveland scores through the air and through Fannin at the goal line.** Six of its eight touchdowns are passes: Fannin from the 2, the 14 and the 2, Boston from 46 and 55, Whiteheart from 17. Fannin has two of the three targets inside the 5. Quinshon Judkins is 59 carries for 177 yards (3.0) with three carries inside the 5, one score and 14 targets in three games. Boston is 0 for 3 inside the 20; Concepcion has no touchdown.
- **The Jets' run defense has broken the last two weeks:** 131 yards to Detroit and 232 to Chicago, with four rushing touchdowns. Their pass defense allows 6.5 yards per attempt, no tight-end score and has nine sacks; Will McDonald IV and Kingsley Enagbare are questionable on the edge. Opponents are 9 of 17 in the red zone against them; Cleveland is 5 of 10.

**Denver made one big move: Jaylen Waddle.** The Broncos sent Miami their first-round pick (No. 30) plus Day 2/3 picks in March for Waddle and a Miami fourth (reports differ on the exact picks: verify), and were the only team not to sign an outside free agent. Bo Nix came back from right-ankle surgery; Davis Webb is the new offensive coordinator, but Sean Payton has taken play-calling back.
- **The depth they drafted is already hurt:** fourth-round back Jonah Coleman (ankle) went to IR before Week 3, and WR Pat Bryant (ankle) went to IR Friday. Denver is 2-2: lost 31-10 at Kansas City and 24-14 at San Francisco, beat Jacksonville 20-13 and the Rams 30-26 on a pick-six.
- **The Chargers rebuilt the offensive staff and are 0-4.** Mike McDaniel was hired as offensive coordinator after last season's playoff exit; Jesse Minter left to coach the Ravens and Chris O'Leary (Western Michigan) is the new defensive coordinator. David Njoku signed a one-year deal and is now on IR.
- **Four losses by 12, 12, 8 and 7,** with 14, 14, 16 and 23 points. Herbert's passer rating is about 70, the lowest among starters.
- **The line has collapsed underneath him:** Rashawn Slater had high-ankle surgery and went to IR Friday, Joe Alt (neck) is out, and guards Trevor Penning and Kayode Awosika are out. This line opened LAC -2.5 and is now DEN -3.5.

- **The Chargers' secondary is short too:** Derwin James Jr. and Donte Jackson are out from a defense allowing 7.9 yards per attempt, 9.7 per target to receivers and six passing touchdowns. Waddle (7.7 targets a game the last three) draws Cam Hart, Deane Leonard and Tarheeb Still.
- **Herbert plays behind a new line.** ESPN's depth chart has rookie tackles Logan Taylor and Travis Burke, with Jake Slaughter, Jacob Spomer and Cole Strange inside. He has 12 sacks, six interceptions and four touchdowns.
- **The receivers are gone too.** Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson are out and Ladd McConkey (foot) did not practice; with Njoku on IR, 47 of the Chargers' 117 targets are unavailable. Tre' Harris (21 targets, 16.1 a catch) and Oronde Gadsden (8 targets last week, a team-high four red-zone looks) are what is left.
- **Omarion Hampton owns the goal line, not the backfield:** all three Chargers rushing scores (from the 8, 1 and 2) and 11 red-zone carries, but Keaton Mitchell led the backs in snaps last week (36.6%) with six targets.
- **Denver is without Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss** (Jahdae Barron, Kris Abrams-Draine, Ja'Quan McMillian cover), has eight sacks and allows 4.76 a carry. Tight ends hurt it: Tyler Higbee 8 for 62 and a score, George Kittle a 56-yard touchdown.

**Arizona is dismantling as it goes.** Kyler Murray was released in the spring and Jacoby Brissett kept the job; Notre Dame's Jeremiyah Love went third overall with Tyler Allgeier signed from Atlanta as the veteran complement; James Conner (foot) and Trey Benson are on IR, rookie corner Will Johnson (neck) is on IR, and on Saturday the Cardinals told Marvin Harrison Jr. he will be inactive while a trade is finalized (Schefter, Rapoport), ending a 13-target, four-game start under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.
- **Detroit's backfield is Jahmyr Gibbs alone:** David Montgomery is off the roster and Isiah Pacheco, signed to complement him, is on IR with a back injury; Gibbs has 80 of the Lions' 98 carries. The receiving tree is unchanged: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta, with second-year Isaac TeSlaa growing into the fourth role.
- **The Lions are 2-2 and 0-2 on the road** (31-30 over New Orleans, 31-41 at Buffalo, 31-24 over the Jets, 26-32 at Carolina), averaging 29.8 points and 405 yards while allowing 31.8 points, second-most in the league. Safeties Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) have yet to play and both remain out.
- **Arizona is 1-3** (26-14 at the Chargers, 7-31 against Seattle, 30-36 at San Francisco, 24-36 at the Giants), averaging 21.8 points on 4.6 yards a play and allowing 29.3. The line has come down about three points toward the Cardinals since it opened.
sections.matchup:
**Jared Goff against the league's worst pass defense, with a Detroit defense that cannot get off the field: the 54.5 is earned.** Arizona has allowed 8.6 yards per attempt and a 114.9 opponent passer rating, about 10.6 yards per target to wide receivers and eight receiver touchdowns in four games, two of them 80-plus yards. Goff is 109 of 161 (67.7%) for 1,214 yards, 9 touchdowns and no interceptions, 412 on 52 throws at Carolina, and Detroit scores touchdowns on 72% of red-zone trips (13 of 18).
- **Gibbs owns the goal line:** all five Lions rushing touchdowns are his, four of them from the 1, plus receiving scores from the 11 twice; 80 of 98 team carries and 28 targets. Arizona has allowed three rushing touchdowns and 4.2 a carry, so his case is volume and the stripe, not efficiency.
- **St. Brown is the red-zone receiver:** five touchdowns (19, 4, 2, 27 and 4 yards) on 46 targets. LaPorta drew 13 targets last week and has scored from the 1 and the 8; Williams has 16 catches at 14.3 a catch and no score against the secondary that gave up the two longest receiver touchdowns in the league; TeSlaa (4 of 8 for 95, 3 of 3 for 66) is the deep fourth option.
- **Detroit's defense is the leak on the other side, and it runs through the tight end.** Opponents have scored touchdowns on 14 of 17 red-zone trips (82%) and 31.8 points a game; six of the 17 offensive touchdowns allowed went to tight ends (Juwan Johnson, Fant, Knox, Kincaid, Sadiq, Ruckert), who average 12.5 targets and 102 yards a game against the Lions. Branch and Joseph have yet to play, Ya-Sin is out, and D.J. Reed grades 57.5 in coverage at PFF.
- **McBride and Wilson are the Arizona passing game:** McBride 33 of 46 targets for 242 with scores from the 3 and the 2; Wilson 25 of 44 for 258, 11 of 17 and 7 of 13 the last two weeks. Harrison's 13 targets (3, 1, 5, 4) and one score go to Kendrick Bourne (8 of 8 in Week 1), Reggie Virgil and two-tight-end sets with Elijah Higgins, who scored from the 2 last week with Hunter Long now on IR.
- **Brissett throws short and often:** 103 of 152 for 818, 5.4 a throw, 6 touchdowns, 4 picks (3 at the Giants), 52 attempts at San Francisco. Love (55 for 223; 21-90 in Week 3, 14-63 last week with his snaps managed around an ankle) has the carries from the 5 and in; Allgeier (32-112) took the 22-yard score last week; Brissett took the sneaks from the 1 in Week 3 and scored.
- **Arizona's protection is patched:** Paris Johnson Jr. to IR Tuesday, Isaiah Adams out, Jon Gaines II at right guard, Jedrick Wills Jr. signed off Buffalo's practice squad. Detroit has 15 sacks, Aidan Hutchinson leading.

**Houston traded for David Montgomery and is 0-4 anyway.** The Lions sent Montgomery to Houston this offseason for a 2026 fourth, a 2027 seventh and lineman Juice Scruggs; Reed Blankenship signed from Philadelphia on a three-year deal to pair with Derek Stingley Jr.; C.J. Stroud is playing without an extension. Houston went 12-5 and reached the divisional round for the third straight year under DeMeco Ryans, and has now lost three games by a combined 11 points.
- **Ryans took the defensive play-calling back from Matt Burke on Wednesday:** the unit is 26th in points allowed (27.3) and has given up late go-ahead drives in three of four games.
- **The receiver room is thinner than planned:** Tank Dell (2024 ACL/MCL) is out again, Jayden Higgins is on IR, and Nico Collins missed Weeks 2 and 3 with a grade 1 hamstring strain before returning for 7-118-2 against Dallas. OT Braden Smith (foot) and rookie DT Kayden McDonald (ankle) are on IR but practiced fully Thursday and are listed questionable (activation: verify); CB Jaylin Smith went to IR Tuesday.
- **Tennessee hired Robert Saleh in January** after a second straight 3-14 season; Brian Daboll is reported as his offensive coordinator (verify). The Titans took Ohio State receiver Carnell Tate fourth overall (22 catches and 268 yards, the rookie lead in catches), and former Giants Wan'Dale Robinson and Daniel Bellinger are in the pass game. Calvin Ridley has five targets in four games. Rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr. has 42 tackles, third in the league.
- **Series:** Houston has won three straight and six of seven, 23-0 and 16-13 last season, and Cam Ward was sacked six times in each. Tennessee has lost 10 straight AFC South games.

**Pittsburgh is in year one under Mike McCarthy, with Aaron Rodgers back and the Colts' old WR1 in black and gold.** The Steelers traded for Michael Pittman Jr. from Indianapolis, signed Rico Dowdle on a two-year deal to split the backfield with Jaylen Warren (Kenneth Gainwell left for Tampa Bay), and hired Patrick Graham from the Raiders as defensive coordinator (verify). McCarthy is 2-2: wins over Atlanta and Cincinnati, losses at New England (20-3) and at Cleveland on Thursday night (27-24).
- **The secondary has been rebuilt on the fly:** Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas (verify), Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. came in at corner, rookies Daylen Everette (CB) and Robert Spears-Jennings (S) are starting, Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith were signed this week, and DT Derrick Harmon (foot) went to IR Monday.

Lou Anarumo runs the defense, with Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward at corner and a rookie-heavy front seven (CJ Allen, Bryce Boettcher, Caden Curry, George Gumbs Jr.).
- **The Colts' season so far:** 41-23 loss to Baltimore, 33-30 overtime loss at Kansas City, 19-17 over Houston, 30-13 over Washington's third-string quarterback in London. They return from the London trip without a bye.

**Jonathan Taylor against a Steelers defense that has allowed five red-zone trips in four games is the whole game.** Taylor has 86 carries for 353 yards and 6 touchdowns, all seven of the Colts' running-back carries from inside the 5 (five scored), and 21 carries a game; Indianapolis is 9 of 12 in the red zone (75%, 6th) and the only team to score on every trip. Pittsburgh has let opponents inside its 20 just five times (3 touchdowns), allows 4.3 a carry, but gave up 136 rushing to New England and 112 to Cleveland, and now plays without Derrick Harmon.
- **Daniel Jones is why the total is 43.5.** 84 of 132 for 754 yards, 3 touchdowns, 4 picks, 5.7 yards an attempt (30th), 143 yards on 34 throws in London; the Colts are 31st in yards per play (4.6) and 32nd in turnover margin (-6). Pittsburgh's rush (10 sacks, T.J. Watt 4.5, Alex Highsmith 3) and 8 takeaways (2nd) meet a quarterback with eight giveaways. Jones keeps a goal-line role: a 4-yard touchdown run from the 4 last week, 11 carries on the season.
- **The Colts' tree is Downs, Warren and Allen, and only Warren and Allen get the inside-10 looks.** Josh Downs has 28 targets (17 catches, 202 yards), five red-zone targets and none inside the 10. Tyler Warren has 27 targets, 23 catches (85%), scores from the 9 and the 1, and 5-plus catches three straight weeks. Keenan Allen (groin, questionable, full Friday) has three inside-10 targets in three games and the 6-yard score against Houston. With Ashton Dulin and Darius Slayton out and Alec Pierce on IR, Laquon Treadwell is the listed WR1 and took 6 targets last week.
- **Pittsburgh throws a lot and finishes nothing:** 38.8 attempts a game (7th), 21.5 rushes (30th), zero rushing touchdowns, 4 of 9 in the red zone (44%, 29th), 32% on third down (28th), 13 sacks allowed (2nd most), and not one rush from inside the 5 all season; Rodgers has been sacked at the 4 and the 5. He is 88 of 153 (56.8%) for 999 yards, 7 touchdowns and 4 picks, with 292 and 299 the last two weeks.
- **That meets a Colts defense that bleeds yards:** 392 a game, 8.1 yards an attempt and 4.8 a carry allowed, 26 points a game, one interception. Jackson and Mahomes threw for 324 and 382; Washington's third-stringer had 232. Indianapolis has allowed 8 touchdowns on 14 red-zone trips (57%) and 52 tight-end yards a game (Kelce 101, Andrews 49). Arden Key is on IR, Jaylon Carlies is out, and DeForest Buckner (3 sacks) rested Friday. Sauce Gardner draws DK Metcalf.
- **Jaylen Warren is the one Steeler with volume:** 17 carries for 127 and 93 the last two games with Rico Dowdle out, 55 for 309 (5.6) and 13 catches on 20 targets, 27-plus receiving yards every week. Dowdle (toe) was limited all week and is questionable; if he plays he takes early downs, not passing downs. Metcalf has 33 targets but a 48.5% catch rate and one red-zone look; Roman Wilson has exactly 6 targets in all four games; Pat Freiermuth has both inside-10 targets (both touchdowns); Darnell Washington is the listed TE1 and had three incompletions from the 11 last week.
- **Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is out multiple weeks.** In the one game he missed, Germie Bernard ran 86% of the routes and took 8 targets. Pittsburgh's own secondary is thin: Jamel Dean out, DeShon Elliott on IR, Jalen Ramsey (wrist fracture) questionable, rookie Daylen Everette starting.

Earlier in the week: Pittsburgh -1.5 and 44.5 (TeamRankings, Oct 4), DraftKings -2.5 / 44.5 (over -108, under -112) with -135 / +114 (SI Betting), FanDuel -2.5 / 43.5 with -142 / +120 (FanDuel Research), and one Steelers preview says the total has fallen from 47.5 (verify). The move toward Pittsburgh came with Dulin and Slayton out and the Colts' London return; the total has gone down the whole way.

- Implied team totals: 23.25 Pittsburgh, 20.25 Indianapolis.
- The desk projects 23-20 Pittsburgh, which is the number. The side is a 1: Indianapolis +3 gets the key number and push protection, the Colts are 3-1 against the spread to Pittsburgh's 2-2, Rodgers has been sacked 13 times behind a line that gave up five at Cleveland, and the Steelers are 4 of 9 in the red zone; the case for Pittsburgh is ten days' rest against a team back from London with a quarterback at 5.7 yards an attempt and eight giveaways. Tyler Warren +215 (31.7% vs 31%). Roman Wilson +290 (25.6% vs 24%). Darnell Washington +400 (20% vs 19%). Daniel Jones +650 (13.3% vs 12%): one carry from inside the 5 all year, it scored. DK Metcalf +160 (38.5% vs 33%): one red-zone target in four games, a 48.5% catch rate, and Sauce Gardner. Josh Downs +230 (30.3% vs 25%): five red-zone targets, none inside the 10. Germie Bernard +400 (20% vs 17%): the route bump is real, the red-zone role is two targets, one of them an interception.

sections.offseason:
**Las Vegas rebuilt the league's worst 2025 offense around a veteran bridge and a rookie in waiting.** First-year coach Klint Kubiak got Kirk Cousins in free agency, took Indiana's Fernando Mendoza first overall (Kubiak has said Mendoza starts when his own play earns it; he has not taken a regular-season snap), and gave center Tyler Linderbaum the richest contract ever for an interior lineman.
- **It has worked so far:** 3-1 and 4-0 against the spread, 28.8 points a game. Cousins is 93 of 144 for 1,026 yards, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, sacked five times, and was the first quarterback since Russell Wilson in 2020 to open 3-0 with three touchdown passes in each win. The 30-27 loss to Kansas City was a 52-attempt, 365-yard game.
- **The receiver room has thinned every week:** Jack Bech (forearm) went to IR after Week 2, Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is on IR, and Jalen Nailor is out with a concussion (he was hurt on a second-quarter play against the Chiefs). Brock Bowers missed Weeks 1-2 with the knee and has 25 targets in the two games since.
- **New England opened with a Super Bowl LX rematch at Seattle and lost 13-10,** then beat Pittsburgh 20-3, lost 35-6 at Jacksonville and won 29-26 at Buffalo. The Patriots signed Romeo Doubs in March (four years, $68 million per Albert Breer) and sent a 2028 first and a 2027 fifth to Philadelphia for A.J. Brown on June 1; Brown caught three passes in the opener and is on IR with the ankle.
- Drake Maye is 73 of 117 for 854 yards, 4 touchdowns and 7 interceptions, sacked 10 times, with 23 runs for 136. Harold Landry III is on a reserve list and guards Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten are on IR.

**New England plays Cousins without its top four corners.** Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) also missed Week 4; Carlton Davis III (neck), Karon Prunty and Channing Canada (hamstrings) join him. ESPN's depth chart lists only nickel Marcus Jones and Charles Woods (questionable) behind them. Without Gonzalez at Buffalo, Keon Coleman had 116 yards and Khalil Shakir 82.
- **Las Vegas scores through the air:** 11 of its 12 offensive touchdowns are passes, 8 of 15 red-zone trips ended in touchdowns. Cody White has three scores on 10 targets, all from inside the 13; Bowers two in two games (from the 4 and 20) and four red-zone targets; Jeanty two catches for scores from the 13; Michael Mayer one from the 3.
- **The run game is the weak link, and Jeanty may not play:** 3.1 yards a carry as a team; Jeanty 78 for 264 with no rushing touchdown on six carries from the 5 or closer. Mike Washington Jr. has 24 for 120 and the only rushing score (35 yards at New Orleans). New England allows 4.5 a carry to backs.
- **Tight ends:** Bowers drew 14 and 11 targets, Mayer 10 against Kansas City. No tight end has topped 32 yards against New England, but LB Christian Elliss and S Craig Woodson are questionable.
- **Pressure, Las Vegas side:** New England has 8 sacks, with Landry out and Dre'Mont Jones questionable; Cousins has been sacked 5 times in 149 dropbacks.
- **New England's offense meets a defense that leaks red-zone and tight-end touchdowns:** Las Vegas has allowed touchdowns on 10 of 13 trips and five scores to tight ends (Juwan Johnson twice, Noah Fant twice, Oronde Gadsden), three from inside the 3. Hunter Henry has 15 targets, one inside the 20 and no touchdown; Eli Raridon has two of the Patriots' four targets inside the 3 and scored at Seattle.
- **Patriots red zone 4 of 9.** Doubs has four red-zone targets and both of last week's touchdowns (from the 14 and the 2); Mack Hollins (four red-zone targets) is out. Rhamondre Stevenson has both back carries inside the 5 (a score from the 1); TreVeyon Henderson has the 39-yard score.
- **Pressure, New England side:** Las Vegas has 12 sacks; Maye has been sacked 10 times with 7 interceptions and fumbled three times at Buffalo, and RT Morgan Moses (foot) is questionable. The Raiders give up 16.9 yards a catch to receivers but only 36 catches on 74 targets.

sections.offseason:
**Minnesota bet the season on Kyler Murray and the defense, and so far the defense is winning the games.** Murray signed in free agency and won the job over J.J. McCarthy on Aug. 11, McCarthy was traded to the Giants for a 2027 fifth, and Carson Wentz started Weeks 1 and 2 while Murray was in the concussion protocol. The Vikings are 4-0 and have allowed 51 points with Brian Flores in his fourth year running the defense.
- **The offensive line is coming apart:** LG Donovan Jackson tore a meniscus in Week 4 (IR, expected to miss the rest of the regular season), LT Christian Darrisaw is out with a concussion, RT Brian O'Neill is questionable and C Michael Jurgens is only now back from IR. Ryan Van Demark (seventh career start) and second-year undrafted Joe Huber start on the left side; third-round rookie Caleb Tiernan starts at right tackle if O'Neill sits.
- **The skill group has thinned too:** RB Jordan Mason (thumb) and TE Josh Oliver (biceps) are on IR, Jauan Jennings (one-year deal) has 2 catches on 4 targets, and Odell Beckham Jr. is on the practice squad as receiver insurance.
- **New Orleans is in year two under Kellen Moore, with Tyler Shough as the full-time starter.** The Saints paid Travis Etienne Jr. four years and $52 million (now on IR, hamstring), added TE Noah Fant and G David Edwards, traded for edge Tyree Wilson and let Demario Davis go.
- **First-round LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle surgery) and WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) are on IR,** so Asim Richards plays left tackle. The Saints are 1-3 and on a six-day turnaround after losing 45-24 to Atlanta on Monday night; Minnesota has its bye next week.
sections.matchup:
**Minnesota's offense against the worst defense it has seen is the whole game.** The Vikings are 28th in EPA per play and last in success rate at 4.4 yards a play, with one offensive touchdown in three games: Murray is 42 of 66 for 415 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT and 7 sacks in two starts, no red-zone trip at Tampa and two empty ones against Miami, where Will Reichard kicked five field goals.
- **New Orleans has allowed 32 points a game, is last in points per play and 30th in EPA per play,** and has allowed touchdowns on 12 of 18 red-zone trips. Backs have 554 yards on 106 carries (5.2) and nine rushing scores against it and caught 16 of 17 targets. LB Kaden Elliss and edge Anfernee Jennings are out.
- **That is Aaron Jones Sr.'s game.** With Mason on IR he had 37 of 44 back carries in Murray's starts plus 14 targets, and 6 of the 10 red-zone carries by Vikings backs this year (Mason had the other four).
- **T.J. Hockenson is the red-zone target:** five red-zone looks, a team high, and 13 of 13 for 119 last week with Oliver gone. Tight ends have 29 catches on 39 targets against the Saints. Justin Jefferson (ankle) has 17 targets and both scores came from Wentz; he has not played a full game with Murray.
- **Chase Young (17 pressures, 18.7% rate) lines up over Van Demark on 95% of snaps,** with Huber inside him.
- **Shough leads the league with 180 attempts** (121 for 1,203, 9 TD, 3 INT) and has faced 73 pressures, 12 sacks and five fumbles. Minnesota is third in pressures (74), has 16 sacks, holds passers to 51% completions and has allowed two touchdowns on 11 red-zone trips. Backs average 3.9 a carry against it with one rushing score.
- **The Saints score through tight ends at the goal line:** Juwan Johnson has 10 red-zone looks, five inside the 10 and three scores; Fant has three touchdowns on three red-zone targets; Devaughn Vele six looks and scores from the 1 and 3. Chris Olave leads the NFL with 48 targets and has one score, from the 21. Kamara took both back carries inside the 5 since Etienne's IR move and scored twice; Shough has two carries from the 1.
sections.injuries:
**Friday report (Oct 9): final designations.** Vikings: LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion, three DNPs) and CB Charles Demmings (hamstring) are **Out**. WR Justin Jefferson (ankle; limited all three days) and WR Jordan Addison (hamstring; DNP Wednesday, limited Thursday and Friday) are **Questionable**, as are RT Brian O'Neill (knee, limited all week), C Michael Jurgens (elbow, off IR) and TE Ben Yurosek (ankle, full all week). ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports Jefferson plans to play but the team will test the ankle Saturday; Kevin O'Connell said he "progressed throughout the week," and the Vikings could also hold him to the Week 6 bye. Not confirmed active as of Saturday afternoon: **verify** at the 90-minute inactives.
- **Where Vikings touches go:** without Jefferson in Week 4 Murray's tree was Hockenson 13 targets, Jones 8, Addison 6; Jauan Jennings is the next wideout and Beckham the elevation candidate. If Addison also sits, Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price are the wideouts and Hockenson's share climbs again. Jones keeps the backfield either way; Demond Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas are the change-ups.
- **Saints:** LB Kaden Elliss (calf), edge Anfernee Jennings (knee) and G Jeremiah Wright (concussion) are **Out**. RB Alvin Kamara (back; DNP Wednesday, limited Thursday and Friday), WR Barion Brown (thigh; full Friday), S Julian Blackmon (shoulder), DT Christen Miller (illness, DNP Friday), LB Jaylan Ford and S Lorenzo Styles Jr. (both just designated off IR) are **Questionable**. TE Noah Fant (abdomen) was full Friday and has no designation, nor do Chris Olave (foot), Tyler Shough (left hand) or edge Carl Granderson (ankle).
- **Where Saints touches go:** if Kamara sits, Kendre Miller is the lead back with CJ Donaldson behind him, and Kamara's goal-line work splits Miller first, Shough's sneaks second. Fant's return gives back a three-touchdown red-zone target and trims little from Johnson (7 and 8 targets in Fant's two healthy games). Brown is a returner with no targets this year.
- **On IR:** Vikings RB Jordan Mason (thumb), TE Josh Oliver (biceps), G Donovan Jackson (knee). Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring), LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle), WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring).
- Indoors at the Caesars Superdome; weather is not a factor.

**Washington gets its quarterback back and loses its two best receivers in the same week.** Jayden Daniels dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow in Dallas on September 20; Marcus Mariota beat Seattle 33-31 in his place, then sprained his right MCL early in London, and Athan Kaliakmanis threw 33 times in the 30-13 loss to Indianapolis. Daniels practised fully all week and Dan Quinn confirmed Friday that he starts.
- **The receiver room is gutted:** Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is out, Terry McLaurin (hamstring) missed Week 4 and has not practised, and Jaylin Lane (ankle) went to injured reserve Tuesday. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil (triceps) is still on IR.
- **The backfield was reshuffled:** Austin Ekeler was signed before London and rookie Kaytron Allen was waived Thursday, leaving Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and Ekeler.
- **New York is 3-1 in year one under John Harbaugh** with Jameis Winston starting since Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee surgery after Week 2. J.J. McCarthy, acquired from Minnesota, is the backup; Winston is the starter again this week.
- **The Giants keep losing depth:** Brian Burns (ACL) is on IR, Braxton Berrios (foot) joined him Wednesday, Odell Beckham Jr. was released, and Jake Haener was signed off the practice squad. Andrew Thomas returns at left tackle after missing Week 4.
- Last week New York beat Arizona 36-24 (Winston three touchdown passes, a 98-yard Deonte Banks pick-six); Washington is 1-3 and has allowed 30 or more three times.
sections.matchup:
**Daniels is back, but he is throwing to the third, fourth and fifth receivers in a thunderstorm.** In his game and a half he was 29 of 51 for 260 yards (5.1 a throw), 3 touchdowns, no picks, plus 12 carries for 100 yards. Diggs and McLaurin own 53 of Washington's 129 targets and 4 of its 8 touchdown catches. What is left: Antonio Williams (19 targets, 8 last week, the 1-yard score in Week 1), Dyami Brown (13), Treylon Burks (6, touchdowns the last two weeks) and Chig Okonkwo (7 in two games).
- **The Giants' defence covers but cannot rush.** Three sacks in four games (2.2% of dropbacks) with Burns on IR and Chauncey Golston out, yet 6.2 yards an attempt allowed and tight ends held to 25 of 35 for 172 yards. Backs have 77 receiving yards against it all year. The leak is the run: 4.7 a carry.
- **Washington's run game has been its worst unit.** Croskey-Merritt has 56 carries for 157 yards (2.8; 1.9 and 1.7 the last two weeks) and the 1-yard score; White has 22 for 100. Inside the 10 they have two carries each, and Allen's two are gone. Daniels threw three straight times from the 1 in Dallas.
- **Winston's Giants kick field goals.** In three starts he is 43 of 78 (55%), 479 yards, 3 touchdowns, 3 picks, sacked 9 times; New York is 2 of 7 in the red zone under him, Zvada has 9 field goals, and there has been no rushing touchdown since Week 1.
- **Washington is the defence that can change that.** It allows 30.5 points a game, touchdowns on 12 of 15 red-zone trips, ten passing scores and five to tight ends (Goedert two, Ferguson two, Saubert); tight ends are 19 of 25 for 243 against it. Safeties Nick Cross, Tyler Owens and Percy Butler are all out, so Jeremy Reaves and Quan Martin start, and edge rushers Omenihu and Wise are out. It allows 3.98 a carry.

**Philadelphia rebuilt its passing game and its offensive staff, then lost two more starting linemen this week.** A.J. Brown was traded to New England, Sean Mannion became offensive coordinator and Jeff Stoutland left after 13 seasons as line coach; Hollywood Brown, Riq Woolen, Jonathan Greenard and Tank Bigsby arrived by trade and Vic Fangio stayed as defensive coordinator.
- **The line is gutted:** Lane Johnson retired Tuesday, Cam Jurgens was traded to Baltimore Wednesday, Landon Dickerson is on IR and new center Drew Kendall was ruled out Friday. Rookie right tackle Markel Bell (second start) and second-year guard Willie Lampkin start; Jake Majors is next at center on ESPN's depth chart (verify).
- **The receivers are Dontayvion Wicks (from Green Bay), rookie Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper** with DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown out; Dallas Goedert returns from a Week 2 MCL sprain after two missed games. Zach Ertz reverted to the practice squad.
- **Jacksonville is in year two under Liam Coen** after a 13-4 season, the best in franchise history, and a wild-card loss to Buffalo; the 2025 defense set franchise records for rushing yards allowed (85.6 a game), takeaways (31) and interceptions (22). Daniel Faalele and Ameer Abdullah were added and Jakobi Meyers was kept and named a captain.
- **Coen has moved to more 12 personnel,** which cost Brian Thomas Jr. snaps (23 in Week 3, 38 in Week 4), and Travis Hunter is mostly a corner now (one offensive target all season, an interception in Week 3).
- The Jaguars have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games, arrived in London a day before the Eagles for a 10-day stay and play Houston at Wembley next week; the Eagles were scheduled to land Saturday morning.

Brian Thomas Jr. has 15 targets and one red-zone look (his Week 4 score).
- **Philadelphia's defense is the better half of the team:** 6.55 yards per pass attempt allowed and no tight-end touchdowns, but 4.1 a carry to backs, seven rushing touchdowns allowed (three by quarterbacks) and four sacks in four games. sections.offseason:
**San Francisco rebuilt its receiver room around veterans and got George Kittle back from the Achilles he tore in last January's playoffs.** Mike Evans and a returning Deebo Samuel Sr. are the outside starters and Christian McCaffrey is coming off a 17-game 2025 (1,202 rushing yards, 102 catches, 17 total touchdowns). The depth behind them is gone: Brandon Aiyuk is out, Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling are on IR, and Brandin Cooks, signed off the practice squad before Week 4, is now listed as the third receiver.
- **The 49ers are 4-0 (27-7 at the Rams, 35-13 Miami, 36-30 Arizona, 24-14 Denver)** and have done it with a defense missing Nick Bosa (calf) and most of its interior; 2025 first-rounder Mykel Williams is working back from ACL surgery inside his PUP window.
- **Seattle is the defending Super Bowl champion,** which ended San Francisco's season in last January's divisional round, and brought back Sam Darnold (4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns in 2025), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (119 catches, 1,793 yards, 10 scores), Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, AJ Barner and Mike Macdonald's defense.
- **The Seahawks' backfield has turned over twice.** Zach Charbonnet (12 rushing touchdowns in 2025) is on PUP after ACL surgery and was not activated this week; rookie Jadarian Price went to IR (chest) after Week 3; ex-Packer Emanuel Wilson is the lead back with George Holani behind him, and a Joe Mixon signing fell through at the physical (verify).
- Seattle is 3-1 (13-10 New England, 31-7 at Arizona, 31-33 at Washington, 30-23 Chargers); Drew Lock started Weeks 1 and 2 while Darnold nursed a glute injury.
sections.matchup:
**The 49ers have not allowed a sack in 113 dropbacks, and Seattle has not let a quarterback past 189 passing yards.** Purdy is 79 of 113 for 1,007 yards, 11 touchdowns and 1 interception, and San Francisco is 11 of 13 in the red zone at 30.5 points a game. Seattle allows 246.8 yards and 144.8 net passing yards a game (Maye 178, Brissett 95, Mariota 183, Herbert 189), with 11 sacks (Leonard Williams 3, Derick Hall 2) and 6 interceptions. The leak is the red zone: opponents have only 9 trips but scored touchdowns on 6.
- **McCaffrey owns the goal line.** Nine of San Francisco's ten carries inside the 5 are his and all four of his touchdowns came from the 1; Purdy's 2-yard scramble is the other. Kaelon Black has 6 red-zone carries and none inside the 5. McCaffrey is at 12.5 carries a game and 4.4 a carry, and Seattle allows 3.6 (408 yards on 112 carries).
- **The 49ers' red-zone passing tree is Kittle and Samuel first.** Kittle and Deebo Samuel Sr. have 5 red-zone targets each and Evans 4; Samuel has 2 of the 4 targets inside the 5 (the 1-yard score last week), Kittle has 4 touchdowns from 12, 10, 20 and 56 yards. McCaffrey has 22 targets and 3 in the red zone. Seattle gives tight ends 29 yards a game (19 catches, 116 yards) but both Eli Raridon and Trey McBride scored on it from the 2.
- **Seattle's red zone is Smith-Njigba.** He has 42 of the team's 118 targets, 11 of its 22 red-zone targets, 3 of the 5 inside the 5 and 6 of its 10 passing touchdowns. Barner has 5 red-zone targets, the other 2 inside the 5 and the goal-line direct-snap score; Kupp has 2 and Shaheed none.
- **Seattle's run game is Wilson by default and it has not finished drives.** He had 21 carries for 81 and both touchdowns last week; he has 9 red-zone carries and 3 inside the 5, Holani (questionable) 7 and 3. Seattle's backs have one rushing touchdown in four games and went 0 for 3 from the 1 at Arizona. San Francisco allows 3.7 a carry and two rushing touchdowns.
- **The 49ers' pass rush is thin.** Six sacks (Keion White 2), none against the Rams or Denver, now without Bosa and James Thompson Jr., with S Marques Sigle out and nickel Upton Stout questionable. It has still held opponents to 5 touchdowns on 11 red-zone trips. Seattle is 14 of 45 on third down (31%); San Francisco is 23 of 40 (57.5%).
sections.injuries:
**Friday report (Oct 9): final designations.** 49ers: DE Nick Bosa (knee/calf), DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle), S Marques Sigle (ankle) and FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee, hyperextension and bone bruise, multiple weeks) are **Out** after missing every practice. CB Upton Stout (shoulder, AC sprain) is **Questionable**. DE Mykel Williams (knee) is **Questionable** on the team report while practicing in his PUP window; ESPN's feed carries him as out (verify whether he is activated). WR Mike Evans (ribs) was limited Wednesday and missed Thursday but has **no designation** (Nick Wagoner, ESPN); RB Kaelon Black (illness) was full Thursday and has no designation.
- **Seahawks:** LB Chazz Surratt (calf) and CB Julian Neal (hamstring) are **Out**; RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) stays on PUP and is out. RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is **Questionable** after limited practices Wednesday and Thursday. DT Leonard Williams (ankle, team sack leader) missed Thursday but has no designation and Macdonald called him good to go; S Ty Okada (hamstring) was full and returns; Smith-Njigba's Wednesday absence was rest.
- **On IR:** 49ers WR Christian Kirk (calf; window could open in two weeks), WR Ricky Pearsall, WR Demarcus Robinson, WR De'Zhaun Stribling, TE Jake Tonges; WR Brandon Aiyuk and RB Isaac Guerendo are out. Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest), WR Jake Bobo, FB Robbie Ouzts; WR Irv Charles is practicing off IR and is listed questionable.
- **Where the touches go:** Juszczyk's 6 targets (2 a game) and his short-yardage snaps go to Luke Farrell and Brayden Willis in two-tight-end sets and to McCaffrey; none of it is red-zone volume that moves a top-3 estimate. Price's carries already went to Wilson last week (21 carries to Holani's 7). If Holani sits, his 3 carries inside the 5 go to Wilson, with Velus Jones Jr. and Robert Henry Jr. behind him, and Wilson's role moves from 39% to about 43%.
- **What it moves on defense:** Bosa and Thompson out keeps the 49ers' rush where it was last week (zero sacks of Bo Nix); Sigle out and Stout questionable thin the coverage against Smith-Njigba in the slot. Neal and Surratt are depth losses for Seattle, not starters.
- Weather: 58°F at Lumen Field, gusts to 16 mph, no precipitation in the forecast.
sections.oddsNotes:
**Seattle opened a bigger favourite and the money has come to San Francisco.** ESPN's feed opened SEA -198 / SF +164 on the moneyline; DraftKings is now SEA -3 (-110 both ways), total 45.5 (over -115, under -105), moneylines -162 / +136. Other books quoted this week ran 46.5 to 47.5 on the total (verify), so 45.5 is the low number.
- De-vigged, the DraftKings moneyline is **59.3% Seattle / 40.7% San Francisco**. ESPN's matchup predictor goes the other way at 55.9% for the 49ers; Dimers' simulation has Seattle 58.6% and 25-22.
- Implied team totals: 24.25 Seattle, 21.25 San Francisco.
- The desk projects SEA 23, SF 22. The side is a 1 on SF +3: a one-point projection against a 3, an unbeaten offense that has not been sacked, and an opponent whose backs cannot score from the 1. The move from -198 has already taken some of the value, which is why it is not higher.
- No total call: 45 projected against 45.5. Both defenses argue under (Seattle's 144.8 net passing yards allowed; San Francisco's 5 of 11 in the red zone), and the 49ers' 85% red-zone rate and thin defensive front argue over.
- DraftKings main player lines from the pull: Purdy 226.5 passing, Darnold 234.5, McCaffrey 50.5 rushing, Wilson 64.5, Smith-Njigba 97.5 receiving, Kittle 54.5, Evans 49.5, Samuel 34.5, Barner 22.5.
- Last week on these teams: SF -3 won and Kittle's touchdown cashed, but Purdy over 234.5 lost at 218; in Seattle, SEA -7 pushed, Under 42.5 lost in a 53-point game, Darnold over 232.5 lost at 168 and Smith-Njigba over 7.5 catches lost at 5.

- **2+ touchdowns:** McCaffrey 14% vs +480 (17.2%), Smith-Njigba 12% vs +600 (14.3%), Wilson 9% vs +500 (16.7%), Kittle 6% vs +1500 (6.3%). Nothing clears its price; the desk went 2 for 48 on 2+ tickets in Week 4.

slateTop.why: Twenty-five targets in two games since the knee (14 and 11), touchdowns from the 4 and the 20, four red-zone targets and two of Las Vegas's four named targets inside the 10 in that span. Eleven of the Raiders' 12 offensive touchdowns are passes, and with Jeanty a DNP Friday the red-zone offense runs through him even more. New England has not let a tight end top 32 yards, but its linebacker and safety are questionable and the corners behind them are gone. DK's +140 (41.7%) is close to a 39% role read: a lineup piece, not an overlay; the 2+ at +1000 (9.1%) is fair.

slateValue.name: Darius Cooper

slateValue.name: Noah Fant
slateValue.why: Three touchdowns on three red-zone targets (from the 8, 3 and 16) in his two healthy games, inactive Week 4 with the abdomen and a full practice Friday with no designation. Nine of the Saints' 13 touchdowns have been thrown, and Fant is the second tight end in a tight-end-heavy goal-line tree. FanDuel's +800 (11.1%) against a 15% read; the risk is a snap count trimmed on his return.

slateValue.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
slateValue.why: Tennessee's short-area receiver: 4 red-zone targets, 3 inside the 10, 2 inside the 5, and both Titans receiving touchdowns of the last two weeks (4 and 3 yards). Houston has allowed six receiver touchdowns, Keenan Allen's 6-yarder among them, and Tennessee will be throwing from behind. If Tate's back limits him, Robinson is the first target to move up. FanDuel's +490 (16.9%) against a 21% read is the best price-to-role gap on the board.

Chicago has run 15 running-back carries inside the 5 in four games and Green Bay has allowed seven rushing touchdowns, all to backs. About 8 carries and a share of the short-yardage work reads 20% against +500 (16.7%) at both books.

slateValue.name: Juwan Johnson
slateValue.why: The Saints' red-zone tree runs through him: 10 red-zone looks by the desk's play-by-play count (two drew pass interference), five inside the 10, and three touchdowns from the 9, 2 and 1. 27 targets in four games, and Minnesota's defense, stingy everywhere else, has allowed 7.9 yards a target to tight ends (198 yards on 25 targets). Fant's return trims little: Johnson saw 7 and 8 targets in Fant's two healthy games. +320 at both books (23.8%) against a 27% read is the best price-to-role gap on the board.

slateValue.name: Pat Freiermuth
slateValue.why: Both Steelers targets inside the 10 this season were his and both scored (6 yards against Atlanta, 3 against Cleveland); 5 targets in three of four games and 14 catches on 19. Indianapolis allows 52 tight-end yards a game and has given up touchdowns to Kelce and Moreau, and Pittman's absence adds a target. DraftKings' +310 (24.4%) against a 28% read is the best price on the board.

slateValue.name: Keenan Allen
slateValue.why: Three targets inside the 10 in three games, the most on the Colts, including the 6-yard score against Houston; 20 targets in three games before missing London. Questionable (groin) but a full participant Friday, so he is expected to play, and Pittsburgh is without Dean with Ramsey limited. FanDuel's +420 (19.2%) is under a 22% read; the value disappears if he sits, in which case the targets go to Treadwell and Burks.

slateValue.name: Cody White
slateValue.why: Three touchdowns on 10 targets, all from inside the 13 (two at the Chargers, one from the 4 at New Orleans), four red-zone targets, and targets rising 1-2-3-4. Nailor being out puts him in every three-receiver set against a corner room of Marcus Jones and Charles Woods (questionable). The scoring rate will regress, which is why the read is 19% and not higher; DK's +500 (16.7%) still clears it. FanDuel is +480.

slateValue.name: Quinshon Judkins
slateValue.why: Three of Cleveland's four carries inside the 5 this season and the 2-yard score Thursday, plus 14 targets in the last three games, one of them a catch to the Pittsburgh 1. The Jets have allowed four rushing touchdowns and 363 rushing yards in the last two weeks. A 40% role against +165 at DraftKings (37.7%) is a small buy; his 2+ at +1200 FanDuel (7.7%) against a 9% read is the best long price in the game.

slateValue.why: Two touchdowns on three looks inside the 10 (from the 7 against Jacksonville and the 8 against the Rams) as Payton's goal-line tight end, on five targets all season. FanDuel's +1500 (6.3%) against an 8.5% read is the best long price in the game; DraftKings is +1300.
